payload.notes: Start. Open up/right; begin exploring right-hand branch. Track position relative to origin.
At (1,0), right blocked. Move up into a short branch; continue mapping and return if dead end.
At (1,2), a dead end. Move down to retrace toward the junction and continue exploring unexplored branches.
At (1,1), up is the mapped dead end and down retraces. Explore left branch, which leads to an unvisited cell with up and right openings.
At (0,1); left is unexplored while up/down are retraced paths. Explore left branch.
At (0,1) after blocked left attempt. Explore the open up branch; right leads back to the mapped junction.
At (0,1); left is now open and reveals a long unexplored corridor. Continue left to map it and seek the exit.
At (-2,1), continuing left through the long unexplored corridor. Map each cell and watch for openings or exit.
At (-3,1), corridor continues left with unexplored branches. Continue left to explore toward the corridor end and seek the exit.
At (-4,1), continuing left along the corridor. The left side remains unexplored; proceed toward its end before taking the visible downward branch.
At (-5,1), the corridor ends one step left. Probe the endpoint, then backtrack right to the unexplored downward branch.
At the corridor endpoint; take the newly revealed downward branch to continue exploration.
At (-5,0) after descending from the corridor endpoint. The downward branch continues right; explore it while keeping up as the retrace route.
At the junction after moving right. Explore the newly open downward branch; right appears to dead-end and left is mapped corridor.
At (-4,-1). Continue down into the unexplored branch; right is a dead end and left leads back through mapped corridor.
Down is blocked. Explore the open left branch; up retraces the junction.
At (-5,-1), corridor extends left and right. Continue left to explore the unvisited direction; right retraces the mapped route.
At (-6,-1); explore the open upward branch, which appears to be a short dead end. Right retraces the corridor.
At (-6,1) after moving up. The upward cell is a dead end; probe it, then backtrack down to explore the lower branch.
At (-6,2), the upward branch is a dead end. Backtrack down to the junction and continue exploring the remaining lower route.
At (-6,0); upward dead end is explored. Backtrack down through the explored lower corridor toward the junction and remaining branches.
At (-6,0); upward branch is fully explored and dead-ended. Move right back through the corridor toward the central junction to continue searching for the exit.
Returned to the corridor at (-5,-1). The left branch and upper dead end are explored; proceed right toward the central junction and remaining unexplored routes.
At (-4,-1). Left is explored; move up into the remaining branch and map it.
At the junction after moving up. Explore the open downward branch; right is a short dead end, while left retraces the corridor.
At the lower branch cell; left corridor is explored and down is blocked. Return up to the junction, then probe remaining routes.
At the junction; left and down routes are explored. Probe the short right branch for an exit or hidden continuation.
Right branch is a dead end. Return left to the junction and continue systematic exploration.
At the junction; right is a confirmed dead end, while down and left lead to explored corridors. Continue left to retrace and search for any overlooked exit.
At the corridor cell after moving left from the junction. Right retraces the junction; inspect the open upward branch before continuing systematic exploration.
At (-5,1); the downward branch is explored, so retrace right along the corridor toward the central junction and continue searching.
At the horizontal corridor after moving right. Continue right toward the central junction and inspect any remaining branch or exit.
Continue right along the corridor toward the central junction; no exit visible yet.
At the current corridor junction after moving right. Continue right through the remaining unexplored corridor; monitor for an exit or new branch.
At (-1,1), continuing right along the corridor toward the remaining unexplored area. The right cell has a downward branch; proceed right and inspect it next.
At (0,1). Left corridor is explored; right and up are blocked. Move down to retrace to the origin and inspect remaining connected routes.
Back at origin. Up branch and right-up route explored; take right, then investigate its unexplored downward branch.
At (1,0); up is the explored dead-end branch and left returns to the origin. Explore the remaining downward branch.
At (1,-1). Up retraces the origin’s right branch; explore the open left route, whose adjacent cell has a downward opening.
At (0,-1); right returns to the explored branch, while down opens a new corridor. Continue downward to explore it.
At (0,-2), continuing down the newly explored corridor. Inspect the next cell for the exit or branches.
At (0,-2); continue down into the newly explored corridor, checking for the exit or a new branch.
At the lower corridor dead end with up retracing. Explore the open right branch for an exit or continuation.
At the new right-branch cell. Left retraces the lower corridor; explore upward for an exit or continuation.
At a dead-end cell reached via the upward branch. Only down is open, so backtrack to the previous junction and continue systematic exploration.
At the branch cell after backtracking from the dead end. Up is explored; move left to retrace toward the lower corridor and search remaining routes.
At the lower dead end; right branch is explored. Move up to retrace toward the central area and continue searching.
At the vertical corridor cell; down leads to the explored dead end. Move up to retrace toward the central area and inspect any remaining unexplored route.
At (0,-1); down corridor is explored and dead-ended. Move right into the adjacent branch to retrace toward the origin and continue searching.
At (1,-1); both open routes are explored. Move up to retrace toward the origin and reassess the remaining maze.
At the known junction. Up, down, and left routes have been explored; return left toward the origin to systematically retrace the maze.
At origin after returning from the right-side junction. All known branches appear explored without finding the exit; revisit the upward branch for any overlooked continuation.
At (0,1); up and right are blocked, and the left corridor is explored. Move down to return to the origin and reassess known branches.
At origin; previously explored up branch is a dead end. Re-enter the right-side junction to continue searching for an overlooked route.
At right junction; up is a dead end. Re-enter the lower branch and continue systematic search.
At (1,-1); move up to the junction and continue systematic exploration of any overlooked route.
At the right junction after moving up. The upper branch is a dead end; move left toward the origin and continue systematic exploration.
At origin; right-side branches have been exhaustively checked without exit. Revisit the upward branch and continue searching.
At (0,1) after moving up from origin. Down retraces; continue left through the corridor to search for any overlooked exit or branch.
Continue left through the corridor; previously mapped branches may conceal the route to the exit, so systematically revisit the far side.
At (-2,1); continue left along the corridor to inspect the far-side branch and search for the exit.
At (-2,1); take the open downward branch, which has not been directly explored from this corridor position.
Down is blocked; continue left to the corridor endpoint, then take its downward branch.
At the corridor endpoint; move left once more to the cell with the unexplored downward branch, then descend.
At the far corridor endpoint after moving left. The downward branch is open and unexplored; descend to continue searching for the exit.
At the branch below the far corridor endpoint. Down is blocked; right retraces the long corridor. Explore the open upward route for a possible exit or continuation.
At the far endpoint branch; right retraces the corridor. Continue upward through the unexplored route and inspect for the exit.
Up is blocked. Descend to the branch cell below, then continue retracing through the corridor to search for the exit.
At the lower branch cell; up leads to the explored far endpoint and right retraces the long corridor. Continue right, checking for any overlooked exit.
At the junction after moving right. Continue the right-hand exploration by taking the downward branch; retrace if it dead-ends.
At the branch cell; left and down are blocked or explored. Move up to the junction and reassess the remaining routes.
At the junction; right is a confirmed dead end and the lower branch is explored. Move left along the corridor to continue searching for the exit.
At the corridor cell west of the junction; right retraces the junction, while up is the remaining route to inspect again.
At the far corridor endpoint; up and left are blocked. The downward branch is explored, so retrace right through the corridor toward the junction.
At the horizontal corridor after moving right from the far endpoint. Continue right toward the central junction and inspect for any remaining route or exit.
At the corridor west of the junction; continue right toward the central junction and reassess unexplored branches.
At the junction after moving right. The right corridor and left route are explored; take the open downward branch, which has not been directly investigated from this junction.
Down moved successfully into a new cell with open up and right routes. Explore right first to investigate the remaining branch.
At the new cell reached by moving right; left retraces, while down is the unexplored open route. Continue downward and inspect for the exit.
At the newly reached lower cell; up retraces the branch, while left opens toward a corridor. Explore left for an unvisited route or exit.
At the corridor cell; continue left toward the cell with a downward opening, which may reveal an unvisited route.
At the corridor cell after moving left. Right retraces the known route; take the open downward branch to continue exploring for the exit.
Moved down into a new junction. Down continues three cells and is unexplored; right is a known corridor. Continue down to map the remaining route.
At the new junction; continue down through the unexplored route. Track any exit or side branch, using up to backtrack if needed.
At the unexplored lower corridor after moving down. Down remains open and leads to a cell with a right branch; continue downward to investigate it.
Down is blocked at the lower corridor endpoint. Take the open right branch to investigate the remaining route.
At the new right-branch cell. Up leads to a dead end, while down reaches an unexplored junction with multiple openings. Continue down to map it.
At the newly reached junction after moving down. The downward side appears short; explore the open left corridor next while mapping for the exit.
At the junction's left corridor cell. Continue left to explore the remaining corridor and look for the exit.
At the new left-end cell. Left and down are blocked; inspect the open upward branch, then backtrack via down if it dead-ends.
At the upward branch cell; it is a dead end. Backtrack down to the corridor and continue exploring the remaining junction routes.
Backtracked from the dead-end upward branch. Move right along the corridor toward the previously reached junction and continue exploring unvisited branches.
At the corridor cell after backtracking from the dead-end. Move right to the nearby junction and investigate its remaining unexplored branches.
At the junction after moving right. Right and down appear short or dead-ended; explore the open upward branch for an exit or continuation.
At the junction after moving up. The upward branch is a dead end; explore the open left route while retaining down as the backtrack path.
At the newly reached cell after moving left. Down and left are blocked; explore the open upward corridor, which extends several cells and may lead to the exit.
Moved up into the vertical corridor. Continue upward through the unexplored route; down is the backtrack path.
Continue upward through the unexplored vertical corridor; the route remains open for two cells and may lead to the exit.
At the current junction after moving up. Up is blocked; explore the open right branch first, then backtrack to investigate the downward corridor if needed.
At the corridor cell east of the junction. Continue right into the unexplored branch; the next cell has an upward opening that may lead toward the exit.
At the corridor cell east of the junction. Continue right into the unexplored branch, then inspect its upward opening for the exit.
Right was blocked; at the corridor cell, move up into the unexplored branch and inspect for the exit.
Moved up successfully into a cell with open down and left. Explore the left branch while retaining down as the backtrack route.
At the newly reached cell after moving left. Explore the open upward branch first; right provides a possible backtrack or alternate route.
At the junction after moving up. Up is blocked; inspect the right corridor for an overlooked route, using left or down to backtrack if needed.
At the corridor after moving right from the junction. The adjacent right cell has a known downward branch; retrace left toward the junction and continue systematic exploration.
At the junction after moving left. Right and left corridors are mapped; descend through the open branch to continue systematic exploration and search for the exit.
At the lower junction after moving down. Open right appears the best unexplored route; take it and inspect for the exit or continuation.
At the cell reached by moving right. Both left and down are mapped, but descend to retrace through the lower junction and continue systematic search.
At the lower junction after descending. Up retraces the known route; explore the open left corridor toward its endpoint and any remaining branch.
At the horizontal corridor; move left toward the adjacent cell with a downward branch to continue searching.
At the new left cell; down is open with a three-cell sightline and appears unexplored. Explore downward while right retraces the corridor.
At the newly reached junction. Down remains unexplored and extends two cells; continue downward to search for the exit.
Down moved successfully into the vertical route. Continue downward to inspect the next unexplored cell and look for the exit or a new branch.
At the vertical route below the junction. Continue down into the remaining unexplored cell and check for the exit or a new branch.
At the lower corridor cell; down is blocked. Up and right are open, with right leading toward the previously mapped junction. Re-enter that junction and continue searching for any overlooked exit.
Moved right into a junction-like cell. The downward route extends through two cells and is the best remaining direction to investigate; left and up appear to retrace mapped corridors.
At the junction after descending. The left corridor has been explored; inspect the upward branch again for any overlooked continuation or exit.
At the cell reached by moving up from the junction. The upward branch appears to be a short dead end; probe it before backtracking via down.
At the short upward dead end. Only down is open, so backtrack to the junction and continue systematic exploration.
